post.description: Use when you have one company and want its firmographics, funding and headcount. Give it a domain, ticker or social profile if you possibly can - a bare name is the identifier most likely to miss.

pdl_id.description: PDL company id, or a LinkedIn company slug such as `google`. A hard override: sent alongside anything else, every other match input is ignored.

name.description: Company name, for example "Google, Inc.". The weakest identifier by a distance - an ambiguous name answers 404 rather than guessing - so prefer website, ticker or profile whenever you have one.

website.description: Company domain. The most reliable single identifier.

profile.description: Social profile URL, for example linkedin.com/company/google.

location.description: Free-form location. Raises the likelihood of a name match; never sufficient on its own.

street_address.description: Street address, one value. Never sufficient on its own.

locality.description: City, one value. Never sufficient on its own.

region.description: State or region, one value. Never sufficient on its own.

country.description: Country, one value. Never sufficient on its own.

postal_code.description: Postal code, one value. Never sufficient on its own.

min_likelihood.description:
Refuse a match below this confidence, 1-10, default 2. At 2 the match is only 10-30% likely to be the record asked for. Raising it turns a weak match into a 404, which is the cheaper answer: a 404 is free here and a wrong record is not.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 10; default 2.

required.description: Boolean expression over required top-level output fields using AND, OR and parentheses. Fields used as matching inputs cannot also be required. Access depends on the key's field bundles.

data_include.description: Comma-separated schema fields to return, dot notation for subfields, a leading `-` to exclude instead, `""` for none. Use it to reduce response size.

include_if_matched.description:
Return matching inputs: top-level matched for enrichment, or matched_on within Identify candidates.

Provider reference: default false.

titlecase.description:
Return titlecased values. Responses are lowercase otherwise, which matters when the output is shown to a person rather than matched on.

Provider reference: default false.

post.description: Use to find companies by attribute - industry, headcount, funding stage, location - rather than to look one up you can already name. Each returned company costs 50 credits. Smaller pages reduce payload size.

query.description: Elasticsearch 7.7 query object over the company schema. Only term, terms, exists, bool, match, range, match_phrase, wildcard, prefix and match_all are accepted. Any array inside it is capped at 100 elements - a tenth of what the person endpoints allow, so a filter list carried over from there will fail. Send this or sql, never both.

sql.description: `SELECT * FROM company WHERE ...`. Column selection and LIMIT are ignored, and at most 20 LIKE '%...%' terms are allowed. Send this or query, never both.

size.description:
Request 1-2 companies per call, costing 50 credits per returned company. PDL supports 1-100 upstream, but Exchange authorization is capped at 100 credits, so callers must use size 1 or 2.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 1.

scroll_token.description: The scroll_token from the previous response, replayed with the identical query, for the next page. A 404 while scrolling means the results are exhausted, not that the query broke.

titlecase.description:
Return titlecased values. Responses are lowercase otherwise, which matters when the output is shown to a person rather than matched on.

Provider reference: default false.
